description:
FILED s473f (Opus, 2026-09-09).

perl: `my $u; print {$u} "x"` dies "Can't use an undefined value as a symbol
reference"; a CLOSED handle returns undef instead.  PCL returns undef for both.

%p-out-fh-or-fail's docstring recorded this as UNIMPLEMENTABLE, and named the
reason: "%p-forget-fh leaves the variable UNDEFINED after close, so
`print $closed_fh ...` and `my $u; print {$u} ...` arrive here identical.
Separating them needs close() to leave a closed-handle value behind instead of
nothing -- a representation change, not a dispatch fix."

THAT IS EXACTLY WHAT #1233 DID (s473f): a closed lexical keeps its closed
stream, so the two shapes are now distinguishable.  The docstring has been
updated to point here.

WHY IT WAS NOT DONE IN s473f: it is a NEW DIE, so it needs the gate-SET scan
over both populations (the s372 bar) -- a program that today prints nothing and
carries on would start dying.  Check `perl-tests/` and the cpan board for
`print {$undef}` shapes first.
subject: `print {$u} ...` on an UNDEF designator should DIE as perl does -- #1233 removed the blocker
